Anything else arrives by the street door.

LOOK_AT.say: The claims ledger. Every filing in the district, in one book, in one hand.
repeat: Claim One is on the first page and it is one line long.
Six thousand entries after it, and all six thousand are looking for the first one.
A page, if I lean close. Not a word.
Nothing. It has the whole town in it and no opinion about any of it.

overrides.PICK_UP: That's the district. I'd need a bigger coat.

LOOK_AT.say: A pen, chained to the counter. The chain is longer than the counter requires.
repeat: It has been chained since before the chain was needed, or since somebody proved it was.
It writes. I've used it. It's a perfectly good pen on a chain, and it knows it.
The chain, if I touch it.
Nothing. It's chained, and quiet about it.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's chained. That's the entire design.

LOOK_AT.say: A spindle of numbered tickets. I was ninety-one. The dead don't queue, but I've kept my ticket.
A spindle of numbered tickets. I'm ninety-one.
repeat: Ninety-one. The other man is still forty.
I've taken ninety-two, to see. Nobody stopped me. I'm now two people in the queue.
then: There's one other man in the room, and he's forty.

repeat: Still nothing. It's very patient.
Nothing. It waits extremely well.

overrides.PICK_UP: I've got my ticket. Taking the spindle would be a different sort of crime.

LOOK_AT.say: The office clock. It is authoritative and it is wrong.
repeat: Eleven minutes fast, and authoritative about it.
It's the only clock in Consolation that anybody obeys.

LISTEN_TO.say: Running eleven minutes fast. I know because the church bell disagrees with it, and the church bell is half a step flat.
repeat: Ticking. Fast.
Ticking. I've stopped hearing it. It took four days.

overrides.USE: I'm not adjusting the Registrar's clock. I want to. I'm not.

LOOK_AT.say: The archive. Mott's own file is behind this door: the whole of Claim One, not just the blank page.
repeat: Fanshawe wants Claim One kept quiet. I'd like to know what it's being quiet about.

LOOK_AT.say: A door, locked, with a statute posted beside it explaining precisely who may pass through. I am not among them.
repeat: The statute beside it lists four persons who may pass. I'm none of them, and neither is Mr Sump.
Still locked. It's very consistently locked.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is very thick and there is nothing behind it that moves.
repeat: Nothing through the door.
Nothing at all. Whatever's in there isn't moving.

OPEN.say: The executor of the late Mr. Grubb.

then.speaker: sump
then.line: Twenty minutes. The archive closes at four, and so do I.

OPEN.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::## E9 · The archive — Hob is Mott · with `T_EXECUTOR_NAMED`

overrides.OPEN: Locked. It's the only locked door in Consolation.
overrides.PULL: Locked, and it doesn't give at all. I gave it every chance.

LOOK_AT.say: Form 31-D, Certificate of Death: 'to be signed by the assayer of record.' That's Winnie. She's going to love this.
Forms in triplicate, and a sign explaining that the third copy is for the applicant.
repeat: Twelve slots. The third-copy slot is empty in all twelve.
I've taken one of each. It seemed prudent. It wasn't.
then: There is no third copy in any of the slots.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper, settling. It is a sound like a very slow argument.
repeat: Paper, settling.
Nothing. Even the paper's waiting.

overrides.PICK_UP: I've already taken one of each. It didn't help.

LOOK_AT.say: Every claim in the district, pinned and numbered.
repeat: There's no cross on it. I'd hoped for a cross. A big one, in red.
Somebody has put a pin in it and taken the pin out again. There is a hole.
then: Claim One is a rectangle like all the others.

repeat: Paper, flat to the wall.
Nothing. The pins aren't talking.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's pinned to the wall, and it's the only accurate map in town. I'm not going to be the man who changes that.

LOOK_AT.say: A bench along the wall for those waiting. It seats nine.
repeat: The seat is worn at one end only. Everybody sits nearest the window.
I've sat on it. It's a bench, and it's doing what it can.
Nothing.
Nothing. There's nobody on it.

overrides.USE: I sit. The bench seats nine and was built expecting all of them. That's a lot of expectation for one man.

LOOK_AT.say: Somewhere behind that partition is a certificate asserting my death, filed correctly, in perfect order. It is the best-organized thing that has ever happened to me.
A counter built a little too high to lean on comfortably. I've tested this. Repeatedly.
repeat: Worn in a band where four thousand men have rested their forearms and been told to wait.
There's a brass rail along the front. Somebody once expected a crowd.

LISTEN_TO.say: Sump, stamping. Every third document is somebody becoming official. I know the weight of it now.

repeat: The clock, over my shoulder, and nothing from the counter.
Wood, being leaned on. By me. Against advice.

overrides.TALK_TO: I clear my throat at the counter. The counter refers me to the appropriate line.

LOOK_AT.say: Two roped lines, FILING and INQUIRIES, and no line for the deceased. I'd make a fuss, but who'd write it down?
Two roped lines, two signs. FILING and INQUIRIES.
repeat: The ropes have been up long enough to have worn the paint off the posts.
I've stood in both, to be sure. It made no difference to anything.
then: There is nobody in either of them and the ropes are up regardless.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Two empty queues are quieter than one.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all. There is a clock, and there is a man, and that is the whole of it.

overrides.USE: I stand in INQUIRIES, then in FILING. I am the entire queue in both, and I'm still not at the front.

exits.name: THE STREET DOOR
exits.note: Doc 20 reaches Room 7 through the town map, so this is the way back rather than the way in -- and doc 25 writes it, which is why it exists now.

LOOK_AT.say: The door out. It has a bell on a spring that announces everyone.
repeat: The bell has announced me four times today.
Mr Sump hasn't looked up at that bell in years, I'd guess.
The street.
The bell, faintly, still settling.
